html:
SMTO-GWT-0005 — Gateway unauthorized

GUID: 2d18db91-020c-42ae-a7f2-aeb6244668d2
Slug: gateway-authentication-failed
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't prove it is allowed to do this, so the step was blocked. When a Gateway was the one that refused, it did not carry out the request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the clocks on the SMTO computer and the Gateway computer are both set to the correct time automatically. SMTO's proof carries a time stamp, and the Gateway rejects it if the clocks disagree.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on that Gateway's row. If the Gateway was reset, this check lets SMTO connect to it again automatically.
  3. If this happened while signing in to an online account, start the sign-in again and finish the Authorize in browser step without changing that account's settings in between. SMTO refuses a sign-in whose account settings changed, or that waited too long, after it started.
  4. If the Gateway computer was reinstalled or SMTO lost its saved identity, ask the Gateway's manager to reset its pairing on that computer. Only a reset on that computer lets it trust a new SMTO; it never does this automatically.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway's row shows Connected, or the account sign-in finishes, and the task runs without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or that Gateway. Don't reset the Gateway's pairing unless you're sure its trusted SMTO was deliberately replaced.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An authentication check failed: the Gateway rejected the Server's signed proof (pairing, clock, identity or replay state), or a saved sign-in profile, endpoint or sign-in transaction failed validation.

What this means

  • Authentication validation failed: Gateway paths reject missing or invalid controller proofs, while the shared AuthError default also covers private profile, endpoint and transaction validation. The category alone cannot distinguish these producers. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Authentication validation failed: Gateway paths reject missing or invalid controller proofs, while the shared AuthError default also covers private profile, endpoint and transaction validation. The category alone cannot distinguish these producers.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the originating component and retained authentication code before inspecting its paired identity, private profile or transaction state.

How to fix it

  • Read the code in Technical details (for example gateway_authentication_failed, request_timestamp_invalid or gateway_runtime_epoch_stale). For a Gateway, sync both clocks, verify the Server identity under ~/.smto/controller/identity and its pairing receipt, and reset pairing on the Gateway host only after confirming the identity was deliberately replaced. For a sign-in profile, correct the saved profile (type, HTTPS endpoints, callback /api/agent/auth/oauth/callback) or start a new authorization.
  • Correct the indicated authentication prerequisite. For Gateway pairing, reconnect and verify the existing controller; use a local pairing reset only after confirming that identity was deliberately replaced.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The same intended connection or Gateway passes its authentication check without changing target identity.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-GWT-0013 — Gateway identity changed
  • SMTO-GWT-0006 — SMTO got a message from the Gateway it couldn't trust
  • SMTO-GWT-0007 — SMTO couldn't confirm the computer got your stop or input request
